materials.name: Al 6082-T6
materials.spec: BS EN 755-2 / 485-2. Brackets, GSE, non-flight housings. Anodises well.

materials.name: Al 6061-T6
materials.spec: AMS-QQ-A-200/8. Same role as 6082; use whichever your supply chain stocks.

materials.name: Al 2024-T3
materials.spec: AMS-QQ-A-250/4 (clad /5). Skins, ribs. Clad + primed; poor bare corrosion.

materials.name: Al 2219-T87
materials.spec: AMS 4095. THE weldable aerospace aluminium: propellant tanks, pressure shells. Retains toughness at cryo.

materials.name: Al 7075-T6
materials.spec: AMS 4045. Fittings, lugs. SCC-prone in short-transverse: prefer T73 unless stress signs off T6.

materials.name: Al 7075-T73
materials.spec: AMS 4147. ~10% strength traded for far better stress-corrosion resistance. Default for sustained-load fittings.

materials.name: Al 7050-T7451
materials.spec: AMS 4050. Better through-thickness properties than 7075 in heavy plate: machined bulkheads, thick fittings.

materials.name: Al 5083-H111
materials.spec: BS EN 485-2. Welded enclosures, launch/handling equipment, marine defence kit.

materials.name: AlSi10Mg (L-PBF)
materials.spec: Laser powder bed. Manifolds, brackets with internal passages. Needs stress relief + HIP for anything fatigue-critical; specify build orientation on the drawing.

materials.name: Ti-6Al-4V (Gr 5)
materials.spec: AMS 4911 sheet / 4928 bar / 4954 wire. Structure, closures, brackets, pressure parts. Galls: coat or anti-seize.

materials.name: Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Gr 23)
materials.spec: AMS 4931/4956. Extra-low interstitial: lower strength, much better fracture toughness. Use where a damage-tolerance case is required.

materials.name: Ti-6Al-6V-2Sn
materials.spec: AMS 4918. Heavily loaded fittings and lugs where 6-4 is short; poorer weldability and toughness.

materials.name: Ti-5Al-2.5Sn (Gr 6)
materials.spec: AMS 4926. Alpha alloy: excellent weldability and cryogenic toughness. Cryogenic tankage, welded pressure parts.

materials.name: Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo
materials.spec: AMS 4919. Best creep resistance of the common Ti alloys: hot structure, warm gas paths up to ~540 °C.

materials.name: Ti-3Al-2.5V (Gr 9)
materials.spec: AMS 4945 (seamless tube). The standard lightweight tubing alloy for pressurised fluid lines.

materials.name: CP Ti Grade 2
materials.spec: AMS 4902. Formability and corrosion resistance over strength: liners, bellows, ducting, chemical service.

materials.name: Inconel 718
materials.spec: AMS 5662/5663 bar, AMS 5596 sheet. Hot structure, injectors, high-load fasteners, AM chambers. Strongest common Ni alloy but drops off above ~700 °C.

materials.name: Inconel 625
materials.spec: AMS 5599 sheet / 5666 bar. Lower strength than 718 but welds far more reliably and serves hotter: liners, bellows, ducting, cooled structures.

materials.name: Inconel X-750
materials.spec: AMS 5598/5667. Hot springs, seals, fasteners retaining preload at temperature.

materials.name: Waspaloy
materials.spec: AMS 5704/5708. Where 718 runs out of temperature; difficult to machine and weld.

materials.name: Haynes 230
materials.spec: AMS 5878. W + La additions give outstanding oxidation resistance and thermal stability. Hot gas paths, combustor-type hardware.

materials.name: Haynes 188 (Co-base)
materials.spec: AMS 5772. Excellent oxidation + hot strength; classic combustor and hot-gas hardware material.

materials.name: Hastelloy X
materials.spec: AMS 5536. Fabricated hot sheet-metal structure: liners, shrouds, ducting.

materials.name: Monel K-500
materials.spec: AMS 4676. Oxygen-service and seawater hardware; good galling resistance. Note oxygen-compatibility rules before use.

materials.name: A286 (Fe-Ni-Cr)
materials.spec: AMS 5731/5737. The default hot bolt when 718 is overkill: good to ~650-700 °C at a fraction of the cost.

materials.name: 17-4PH (H1025)
materials.spec: AMS 5643. Valve bodies, shafts, fittings. ALWAYS state the H-condition: H900 strongest, H1025/H1075 better SCC and toughness.

materials.name: 15-5PH (H1025)
materials.spec: AMS 5659. Lower delta-ferrite than 17-4: better transverse toughness. Preferred for forgings.

materials.name: 13-8Mo PH (H1000)
materials.spec: AMS 5629. Very high strength with good toughness and SCC resistance: heavily loaded fittings, actuator parts.

materials.name: Custom 465
materials.spec: AMS 5936. Where you need maraging-class strength but must keep corrosion resistance.

materials.name: Stainless 304L
materials.spec: BS EN 10088-3. Ground equipment, non-critical ducting, brackets. Cheap and universally available.

materials.name: Stainless 316L
materials.spec: BS EN 10088-3. Wet systems, fittings, marine. Work-hardens: rigid setup, sharp tools.

materials.name: Stainless 321 / 347
materials.summary: Stabilised austenitic for welded hot parts
materials.spec: AMS 5510 (321) / 5512 (347). Ti- or Nb-stabilised against weld decay: the standard for welded hot ducting and bellows.

materials.name: 21-6-9 (Nitronic 40)
materials.spec: AMS 5561 tube. Standard high-pressure pneumatic/hydraulic tubing alloy; far stronger than 316 with the same weldability.

materials.name: 440C stainless
materials.spec: AMS 5630. Hardened to ~58 HRC for bearings, wear pins, valve seats. Brittle, not for structure.

materials.name: D6AC (AMS 6431)
materials.spec: AMS 6431, VAR melted. Ni-Cr-Mo-V ultra-high-strength steel developed for SRM cases: ~1520 MPa (220 ksi) UTS at the 538 °C double-temper with 60-80 ksi√in toughness. Weld annealed, then heat treat.

materials.name: 15CDV6 (1.7734)
materials.spec: AIR 9160C / W.Nr 1.7734. Low-carbon CrMoV: welds with negligible property loss and no post-weld heat treatment. Widely used for motor cases, pressure vessels, launch structure.

materials.name: Maraging 18Ni-250
materials.spec: AMS 6512 bar/forgings, AMS 6520 sheet. VIM+VAR. Ages at ~480 °C with almost no distortion; welds in annealed state. Classic case and flexure material.

materials.name: Maraging 18Ni-300
materials.spec: AMS 6514. ~280 ksi with good toughness. Also the common metal-AM tool-steel powder. Watch hydrogen and cleanliness.

materials.name: 300M
materials.spec: AMS 6417. Si-modified 4340. Extremely notch- and hydrogen-sensitive: mandatory bake after plating, no sharp corners.

materials.name: AerMet 100
materials.spec: AMS 6532. Best toughness available at ~285 ksi. Expensive; used where fracture control drives the design.

materials.name: HP 9-4-30
materials.spec: AMS 6526. Good weldability at ultra-high strength: welded fittings and cases where D6AC's heat treat is awkward.

materials.name: 4340 / EN24T
materials.spec: AMS 6415 / BS 970 817M40. Shafts, pins, tooling, GSE. Plate or paint; bake after plating.

materials.name: 4130 (25CrMo4)
materials.spec: AMS 6345/6360. Welded structure, test rigs, nozzle shells, tube frames. The cheap weldable option below 15CDV6.

materials.name: S355 structural steel
materials.spec: BS EN 10025-2. Test stands, handling frames, tooling. Never flight hardware.

materials.name: Mg AZ31B-H24
materials.spec: ASTM B90. Lightest structural metal option; 50+ years of use. Poor corrosion and flammability vs the RE alloys: needs full protective treatment.

materials.name: Mg ZE41A-T5
materials.spec: AMS 4439. Pressure-tight castings: gearbox and transmission housings, electronics enclosures. Good damping.

materials.name: Mg WE43 / Elektron 43
materials.spec: AMS 4427 (cast). Y + rare earths: retains strength to ~250 °C and passes FAA flammability testing. Wrought Elektron 43 is in MMPDS with A/B-basis allowables.

materials.name: Mg Elektron 21 (EV31A)
materials.spec: AMS 4429. Better castability and corrosion than ZE41 with good elevated-temperature retention.

materials.name: Mg ZK60A-T5
materials.spec: ASTM B107 extrusion. Best specific strength of the common Mg alloys; not weldable, poor corrosion: protect thoroughly.

materials.name: C-103 Niobium (Nb-10Hf-1Ti)
materials.spec: AMS 7857. Melts ~2470 °C, ductile and formable for a refractory. Oxidises rapidly above ~400 °C in air. MUST be silicide-coated (e.g. R512E). Standard for radiation-cooled upper-stage and thruster nozzle extensions.

materials.name: TZM Molybdenum
materials.spec: ASTM B387. Ti-Zr-Mo. Excellent hot strength and thermal conductivity; needs oxidation coating. Throat inserts, hot valve internals, gas-path hardware.

materials.name: Tungsten / W-25Re
materials.spec: ASTM B760. Melting ~3400 °C and superb erosion resistance: throat inserts. Very heavy and brittle below its DBTT; usually infiltrated (W-Cu), or used as an insert in a lighter structure.

materials.name: Tantalum Ta-10W
materials.spec: ASTM B708. Ductile and weldable at high temperature with outstanding chemical resistance. Very expensive and heavy: reserved for small hot components.

materials.name: Rhenium (with Ir coating)
materials.spec: Iridium-coated rhenium chambers for high-performance apogee/station-keeping thrusters. Cost and supply are the limiting factors, not performance.

materials.name: Bulk graphite (ATJ / POCO)
materials.spec: Low cost, machines easily, and gets stronger with temperature in inert atmosphere. Brittle and low tensile strength: always design in compression with a supporting shell.

materials.name: Carbon-carbon (2D / 3D)
materials.spec: Far tougher than bulk graphite at similar temperature capability, and very light. Oxidises above ~400 °C in air: needs SiC or similar coating for air exposure. Exit cones, throat packages, hot structure.

materials.name: C/SiC ceramic composite
materials.spec: Ceramic matrix gives oxidation resistance carbon-carbon lacks. Hot structure and nozzle components where reusability or air exposure matters.

materials.name: Carbon phenolic (ablative)
materials.spec: The standard SRM nozzle liner. Ablates and chars to form an insulating layer. Define ply/tape wrap angle on the drawing: it governs performance and is a controlled process parameter.

materials.name: Silica phenolic (ablative)
materials.spec: Used for exit-cone and housing insulation where the heat flux is lower than the throat. Cheaper than carbon phenolic; higher erosion rate.

materials.name: EPDM insulation
materials.spec: Filled elastomer bonded to the case interior: insulates the case structure during burn. Bond integrity (and its NDT) is the design-critical item, not the rubber's strength.

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy (filament wound)
materials.spec: IM7/8552-class prepreg or wet wound. Highest structural efficiency available for cases and COPVs, but strength quoted is fibre-direction only. Winding pattern, fibre volume fraction and cure cycle ARE the material: define them, not just 'carbon fibre'.

materials.name: Aramid/epoxy (Kevlar)
materials.spec: Better impact and burst behaviour than carbon, lower stiffness. Historic motor case and COPV overwrap material; absorbs moisture: control the cure and storage.

materials.name: S-glass/epoxy
materials.spec: Cheaper and more forgiving than carbon, heavier and less stiff. Good for lower-performance cases, tooling and test articles.

materials.name: PEEK
materials.spec: Victrex 450G typ. Insulators, seals, wear parts at temperature, cryogenic valve seats. Expensive: small parts only.

materials.name: Vespel SP-1 (polyimide)
materials.spec: Seals, bushings and thermal isolators in hot or vacuum service. Extremely expensive per kg: design for minimum volume.

materials.name: PTFE
materials.spec: Seals, back-up rings, low-friction faces, cryogenic service. Creeps badly under load: never a structural part; consider filled grades.

materials.name: Acetal / POM-C
materials.spec: Wear pads, rollers, jigs, handling fixtures. Machines beautifully; poor bonding. Not for flight hot zones.

materials.name: Nylon PA6 / PA66
materials.spec: Guides, spacers, GSE. Absorbs moisture: dimensions and properties drift; avoid for precision or flight.

materials.name: GRCop-42 (Cu-4Cr-2Nb)
materials.spec: NASA Glenn dispersion-strengthened Cu-Cr-Nb. Higher conductivity and faster L-PBF build than GRCop-84. Regeneratively cooled chamber liners with integral cooling channels. Forms a stable protective oxide instead of blanching.

materials.name: GRCop-84 (Cu-8Cr-4Nb)
materials.spec: Higher Cr2Nb content gives more strength and creep resistance than GRCop-42, at some cost in conductivity. Proven in bimetallic chambers with superalloy jackets.

materials.name: NARloy-Z (Cu-3Ag-0.5Zr)
materials.spec: The forged liner alloy for decades, including the Space Shuttle Main Engine. Silver content and machining waste made it costly; largely superseded by AM GRCop, and it blanches under cyclic oxidation where GRCop does not.

materials.name: AMZIRC (Cu-0.15Zr)
materials.spec: Zirconium copper: very high conductivity, moderate strength. Older liner and heat-exchanger choice; oxidises severely under cyclic conditions compared with GRCop.

materials.name: GRX-810 (NiCoCr ODS)
materials.spec: Oxide-dispersion-strengthened NiCoCr with ~1 wt% Y2O3 nano-oxides, designed for L-PBF. NASA reports roughly twice the strength, far greater creep life and twice the oxidation resistance of conventional printed superalloys at 1093 C, with test data to 1316 C.

materials.name: NASA HR-1
materials.spec: Fe-Ni-Cr alloy developed for high-pressure hydrogen environments: resists hydrogen environment embrittlement where many superalloys do not. Used for AM regeneratively cooled nozzles and hydrogen-side hardware.

materials.name: JBK-75
materials.spec: Modified A286 developed for weldability and hydrogen resistance in propulsion hardware. Common in hydrogen turbomachinery and ducting.

materials.name: Haynes 282
materials.spec: Gamma-prime strengthened but with far better fabricability and weldability than Waspaloy or R-41. Increasingly the choice for hot static structure and manifolds.

materials.name: Rene 41
materials.spec: Classic 1960s-era gamma-prime superalloy: Apollo-era hot structure and fasteners. Very strong hot but prone to strain-age cracking on welding; Haynes 282 is the modern answer.

materials.name: L-605 / Haynes 25
materials.spec: Cobalt-chromium-tungsten. Excellent hot strength and sulphidation resistance, readily formed and welded. Combustor liners, hot ducting, thrust chamber components.

materials.name: Hastelloy C-276
materials.spec: Outstanding resistance to oxidising and reducing media, including wet chlorine and hypochlorite. Propellant handling, ground systems, scrubbers rather than flight structure.

materials.name: Inconel 939
materials.spec: High gamma-prime cast superalloy, now printed. Higher temperature capability than 718 with better oxidation resistance; harder to weld and process.

materials.name: Al-Li 2195
materials.spec: Aluminium-lithium. Roughly 5% lighter and stiffer than 2219 with higher strength: the Shuttle Super Lightweight Tank alloy. Friction stir welded in practice. Anisotropic and needs careful process control.

materials.name: Al-Li 2050 / 2099
materials.spec: Third-generation Al-Li plate and extrusion for launch vehicle structure. Better damage tolerance and less anisotropy than earlier Al-Li grades.

materials.name: 301 stainless (full hard)
materials.spec: Austenitic that work-hardens dramatically. Cheap, weldable, and it gains strength and toughness at cryogenic temperature rather than losing it: the reason stainless is credible for large cryogenic tank structures.

materials.name: 304L / 316L (cryogenic)
materials.spec: Austenitic stainless retains ductility and toughness to liquid-helium temperature with no ductile-brittle transition: the default for cryogenic plumbing, valves and dewars.

materials.name: Invar 36 (FeNi36)
materials.spec: CTE about 1.2 um/m/K near ambient. Composite layup tooling, optical benches and metering structures where thermal stability beats mass.

materials.name: SiC/SiC CMC
materials.spec: Ceramic matrix composite with far better oxidation resistance than carbon-carbon and a fraction of the density of superalloys. Nozzle extensions and reusable hot structure. Very expensive and slow to make.

materials.name: ZrB2-SiC UHTC
materials.spec: Ultra-high-temperature ceramic for leading edges and extreme throat environments. Excellent oxidation resistance above 1800 C but brittle and thermal-shock sensitive.

materials.name: Alumina enhanced thermal barrier
materials.spec: Silica-fibre reusable tile family used for reusable spacecraft thermal protection. Extremely low density and conductivity, but fragile and permeable: always a coated system, never bare.

materials.name: Iridium-coated rhenium
materials.spec: The classic long-life apogee and station-keeping thruster chamber. Rhenium substrate for strength at temperature, iridium liner for oxidation protection. Extraordinarily expensive and slow to fabricate.

materials.name: PICA (phenolic impregnated carbon)
materials.spec: NASA Ames. Density ~0.27 g/cm³ with efficient ablation above 1000 W/cm². Stardust, MSL and Dragon (as PICA-X). Recedes significantly under long-duration or high-pressure heating: excellent for short intense pulses, less so for sustained flux.

materials.name: AVCOAT 5026-39/HC-G
materials.spec: Epoxy-novolac with silica fibres and phenolic microballoons gunned into a fibreglass honeycomb. Apollo and Orion. Good medium-flux insulation but the honeycomb fill is extremely labour intensive.

materials.name: SLA-561V (cork/silicone)
materials.spec: Ground cork, silicone, silica fibres and microballoons packed into phenolic honeycomb. Viking, Pathfinder, MSL backshells. Low-to-medium heat flux only: it melts and ablates readily at high flux.

materials.name: Cork phenolic (Norcoat type)
materials.spec: Cork granules in phenolic. Widely used as external motor and stage insulation and on backshells: cheap, easily bonded and formed to curvature, and it swells rather than spalls.

materials.name: Glass phenolic (ablative)
materials.spec: Glass fabric in phenolic. Cheaper than silica phenolic with slightly lower temperature capability: exit cone and housing insulation where flux is moderate.

materials.name: Reinforced carbon-carbon (RCC)
materials.spec: Coated carbon-carbon for reusable leading edges and nose caps. Needs a SiC conversion coating plus sealant: bare C-C oxidises rapidly above about 400 °C in air.

materials.name: Glidcop AL-15 (Al2O3 DS copper)
materials.spec: Alumina dispersion-strengthened copper. Retains strength after brazing and welding where precipitation-hardened coppers soften: resistance welding electrodes, high heat flux hardware.

materials.name: CuCrZr (C18150)
materials.spec: Precipitation-hardened chromium-zirconium copper. Good balance of conductivity and strength for heat exchangers, electrodes and cooled hardware. Softens if overheated during welding.

materials.name: Beryllium copper C17200
materials.spec: The strongest copper alloy. Non-sparking tools, springs, bushes and bearings. Beryllium dust is a serious health hazard: machining requires controls.

materials.name: Beryllium (S-200F)
materials.spec: Specific stiffness roughly six times aluminium: optical benches, inertial platforms, mirrors. Brittle, notch sensitive, and the dust is acutely toxic; machining needs dedicated facilities.

materials.name: AlBeMet AM162 (Al-62Be)
materials.spec: 62% beryllium in an aluminium matrix. Roughly three times the specific stiffness of aluminium while machining and joining far more like a conventional metal than pure beryllium. Still a beryllium hazard.

materials.name: Mg AZ80A-T5
materials.spec: Stronger than AZ31 for extrusions and forgings. Same magnesium caveats: galvanic corrosion, flammable swarf, needs full protective treatment.

materials.name: Al-SiC MMC (AMC225xe)
materials.spec: Silicon carbide particulate in an aluminium matrix. Much stiffer and more wear resistant than aluminium with a lower CTE. Very abrasive to tooling. PCD cutters and grinding.

materials.name: Inconel 617
materials.spec: Solid-solution strengthened, excellent oxidation and carburisation resistance to 1100 °C. Combustor liners, ducting and hot gas structure where creep strength matters more than yield.

materials.name: Haynes 214
materials.spec: Forms a protective alumina scale rather than chromia, giving outstanding oxidation resistance above 950 °C where chromia formers fail. Honeycomb seals, combustor hardware.

materials.name: MAR-M-247
materials.spec: High gamma-prime cast nickel superalloy for turbine blades and hot rotating parts. Essentially unweldable and requires investment casting or AM plus HIP.

materials.name: CMSX-4 (single crystal)
materials.spec: Second-generation single crystal: no grain boundaries at all, so no grain-boundary creep or cracking. The highest temperature capability in a metallic blade, at extreme cost and lead time.

materials.name: MA956 (ODS FeCrAl)
materials.spec: Yttria-dispersed FeCrAl. Exceptional oxidation resistance and creep strength to 1300 °C at notably low density for its class. Cannot be fusion welded without destroying the dispersion.

materials.name: Nimonic 105
materials.spec: Gamma-prime strengthened Nimonic for turbine blades and hot fasteners. Common on legacy UK engine drawings.

materials.name: Gamma TiAl (Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb)
materials.spec: Intermetallic with roughly half the density of nickel superalloys at comparable temperature capability: low-pressure turbine blades. Brittle at room temperature and very difficult to machine or join.

materials.name: IMI 550 (Ti-4Al-4Mo-2Sn-0.5Si)
materials.spec: UK alpha-beta alloy for forged compressor discs and highly loaded fittings: stronger than Ti-6Al-4V up to about 400 °C.

materials.name: IMI 834 (near-alpha)
materials.spec: Ti-5.8Al-4Sn-3.5Zr-0.7Nb-0.5Mo-0.35Si. UK near-alpha alloy for compressor discs and blades to about 600 °C.

materials.name: Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al (STA)
materials.spec: AMS 4983/4984. Helicopter rotor hubs and landing-gear parts: deep hardening with high toughness.

materials.name: Nb-1Zr
materials.spec: More ductile and readily welded than C-103, with lower strength. Space nuclear and heat-pipe hardware, and thruster components where formability matters.

materials.name: Tungsten heavy alloy (90W-Ni-Fe)
materials.spec: Liquid-phase sintered tungsten in a nickel-iron matrix. Far more machinable and tougher than pure tungsten. Balance masses, ballast, inertia weights and radiation shielding.

materials.name: Silicon carbide (sintered)
materials.spec: Very hard, stiff and erosion resistant with good thermal conductivity for a ceramic. Seal faces, nozzles, wear parts. Brittle and only ground, never machined.

materials.name: Silicon nitride (Si3N4)
materials.spec: The toughest common structural ceramic with excellent thermal shock resistance. Hybrid bearings, hot rollers, valve components.

materials.name: Zirconia (YSZ, TBC)
materials.spec: Very low thermal conductivity: the standard thermal barrier coating on hot-section components. Tough for a ceramic but heavy, and it sinters and spalls over long exposure.

materials.name: 9% Ni cryogenic steel
materials.spec: Retains toughness to about −196 °C, which most ferritic steels cannot. LNG tanks and cryogenic pressure vessels where austenitic stainless is unaffordable.

materials.name: 17-7PH stainless
materials.spec: Semi-austenitic PH stainless supplied formable then hardened: the go-to for high-strength stainless springs, clips, diaphragms and formed sheet parts.

materials.name: Nitronic 60 (S21800)
materials.spec: Silicon-manganese austenitic with genuinely excellent galling and wear resistance: the answer to stainless-on-stainless seizure in valve stems, fasteners and sliding fits.

materials.name: Custom 455 stainless
materials.spec: Very high strength PH stainless that machines better than most at this strength level. Shafts, fasteners and highly loaded fittings needing corrosion resistance.

materials.name: T800 carbon/epoxy
materials.spec: Intermediate-modulus carbon at high strength: the current standard for filament-wound pressure vessels and motor cases. Higher strain to failure than high-modulus fibres, which is what a pressure vessel needs.

materials.name: M55J high-modulus carbon/epoxy
materials.spec: Very high modulus fibre for stiffness- and stability-critical structure: antenna booms, optical benches, metering structures. Low strain to failure, so poor for pressure vessels.

materials.name: Zylon PBO/epoxy
materials.spec: The highest specific strength available in an overwrap fibre. Used where mass fraction dominates, but it degrades with UV and humidity over time: the ageing behaviour must be designed for.

materials.name: Boron/epoxy
materials.spec: Boron fibre on a tungsten core. Very high compressive strength and stiffness, historically used for repair patches and legacy airframe reinforcement. Expensive and difficult to cut.

materials.name: FKM / Viton (75 Shore A)
materials.spec: Wide chemical range with high temperature capability. Standard grades stiffen around −20 °C: check the cold end before assuming it works. Not for steam, ketones, amines or phosphate esters.

materials.name: FFKM / Kalrez
materials.spec: Near-universal chemical resistance and the highest temperature elastomer available. Priced per seal. Poor low-temperature flexibility.

materials.name: EPDM
materials.spec: The correct choice for Skydrol, brake fluid, hot water and steam, and the workhorse solid motor insulation elastomer. Completely unsuitable for mineral oils and fuels.

materials.name: NBR / Nitrile
materials.spec: The default cheap seal for mineral oil, fuel and grease. Poor ozone and UV resistance: it cracks in storage. Not for phosphate esters.

materials.name: Silicone / VMQ
materials.spec: Widest temperature range of the common elastomers, roughly −60 to +230 °C. Static duty only: poor tear and abrasion strength. Silicone contamination destroys adjacent adhesive bonds.

materials.name: Fluorosilicone / FVMQ
materials.spec: Silicone's cold capability with fuel resistance: the classic aerospace fuel seal for cold environments. Mechanically weak, static duty.

materials.name: Butyl / IIR
materials.spec: Exceptionally low gas permeability: the vacuum and gas-retention choice. Not for hydrocarbons. Poor rebound, which is why it damps well.

materials.name: Polyurethane / AU
materials.spec: Outstanding abrasion and extrusion resistance: the high-pressure hydraulic choice. Hydrolyses in hot humid conditions; polyether grades resist this better than polyester.

materials.name: Neoprene / CR
materials.spec: Good all-round weather and ozone resistance; common in refrigerants and marine service. Usually beaten by NBR on oil or EPDM on water.

materials.name: Aflas / FEPM
materials.spec: Resists steam, amines and strong bases where FKM fails. Oilfield and chemical process favourite. Very poor low-temperature flexibility.

materials.name: Natural rubber / NR
materials.spec: Best resilience and fatigue behaviour of the common elastomers: vibration mounts and flexible couplings. Poor oil, ozone and temperature resistance.

materials.name: EPDM insulation (silica filled)
materials.spec: Filled EPDM is the workhorse internal insulation for composite propellant motors. The bond to case and propellant is structural: that, not the rubber's own strength, is the design driver.

materials.name: PEI / Ultem 1000
materials.spec: Excellent flame, smoke and toxicity performance: a cabin interior staple. Attacked by chlorinated solvents and some paint strippers.

materials.name: PAI / Torlon
materials.spec: Highest strength and stiffness of any melt-processable polymer, with outstanding wear behaviour under load and heat. Needs a long, costly post-cure.

materials.name: PPS / Ryton
materials.spec: No known solvent below 200 °C. Inherently flame retardant. Brittle unfilled: almost always glass or carbon filled.

materials.name: PCTFE / Kel-F
materials.spec: Lowest gas permeability of the fluoropolymers and excellent cryogenic performance: a classic LOX-service seat material. Less cold flow than PTFE.

materials.name: UHMWPE
materials.spec: Outstanding abrasion resistance, better than many metals, with very low friction. Creeps under load and cannot be bonded conventionally.

materials.name: Al 1050A (pure)
materials.spec: Commercially pure. Excellent formability and corrosion resistance, very low strength. EN 485-2 sheet, EN 755-2 extrusion.

materials.name: Al 2014A-T6
materials.spec: High-strength Cu-bearing forging alloy. Legacy UK 'L' specs (L168) still appear on heritage drawings. Poor corrosion resistance bare.

materials.name: Al 6063-T6
materials.spec: Lower strength than 6082 but far better extrudability and surface finish. The architectural and heat-sink extrusion alloy.

materials.name: Al 7020-T6
materials.spec: Weldable 7xxx that age-hardens naturally after welding, recovering HAZ strength. Susceptible to stress-corrosion: control temper and avoid sustained short-transverse tension.

materials.name: Al A356 / LM25 (cast)
materials.spec: The workhorse aluminium casting alloy. Good castability and pressure tightness, weldable, heat treatable to T6.

materials.name: Al 7010-T7451
materials.spec: AMS 4204 plate. Machined frames, spars and fittings: good through-thickness properties and stress-corrosion resistance in the T7451 temper.

materials.name: Al 2618A-T61 (RR58)
materials.spec: AMS 4132 forgings (RR58). Keeps its strength to about 200 °C: compressor parts, pistons, the Concorde skin. Machines well; not weldable.

materials.name: Al 5251-H22
materials.spec: BS EN 485 sheet. Panels, covers, ducting and tanks. Good corrosion resistance and formability; weldable.

materials.name: Mg AZ91 (die cast)
materials.spec: The dominant magnesium die-casting alloy. Good castability and strength; poor corrosion resistance without full protective treatment.

materials.name: 4140 (42CrMo4)
materials.spec: The general-purpose through-hardening alloy steel. Shafts, tooling, high-strength fittings. Weldable with preheat and PWHT.

materials.name: Tool steel H13
materials.spec: Hot-work die and mould steel with excellent thermal fatigue resistance. Also a common AM tool steel. Air hardening, minimal distortion.

materials.name: Tool steel D2
materials.spec: High-carbon high-chromium cold-work die steel. Outstanding wear resistance and edge retention, poor toughness: chips rather than bends.

materials.name: Tool steel O1
materials.spec: Oil-hardening non-shrinking tool steel for gauges, jigs and fixtures. Easy to machine annealed, stable through heat treatment.

materials.name: Grey cast iron (EN-GJL-250)
materials.spec: Excellent vibration damping and machinability, very low cost. Brittle in tension. Machine bases, housings, damping-critical tooling.

materials.name: EN3B mild steel (bright drawn)
materials.spec: BS 970 070M20 / 230M07 range (EN3B), bright drawn. Jigs, brackets, spacers and ground equipment. Never flight hardware. Bright-drawn strength varies with the bar size: use the certificate.

materials.name: EN8 (080M40), normalised
materials.spec: BS 970 080M40 (EN8), normalised. Shafts, studs, axles and ground equipment; induction or flame hardens. 0.4% carbon: weld only with preheat and a procedure.

materials.name: EN16T (605M36)
materials.spec: BS 970 605M36 (EN16), condition T. Shafts, axles, high-tensile studs and bolts for ground equipment. Through-hardens in moderate sections.

materials.name: Stainless 410
materials.spec: Hardenable 12% chromium martensitic stainless. Turbine blades, valve parts, fasteners. Corrosion resistance well below austenitic grades.

materials.name: Duplex 2205
materials.spec: Ferritic-austenitic duplex with roughly double the yield of 316L and far better chloride stress-corrosion resistance. Limited above 300 °C by embrittlement.

materials.name: 431 stainless (S80)
materials.spec: BS S80 / AMS 5628 (431, 1.4057), hardened and tempered. Shafts, pins, valve parts and fasteners. The best corrosion resistance of the martensitic grades; avoid the temper-embrittlement range.

materials.name: 303 stainless (free machining)
materials.spec: BS EN 10088-3 1.4305. Turned fittings, spacers and screws. The sulphur that makes it machine lowers its corrosion resistance and weldability: not for welded, marine or oxygen parts.

materials.name: FV520B (1.4594)
materials.spec: Precipitation-hardening martensitic stainless (1.4594). Compressor and turbine parts, shafts, highly loaded fittings. Weldable, with a post-weld heat treatment.

materials.name: Super duplex 2507 (1.4410)
materials.spec: ASTM A240 S32750 / 1.4410. Seawater, chloride and sour service: marine test equipment, coolant and process pipework. PREN above 40. Limited to about 250 °C by 475 °C embrittlement over time.

materials.name: Kovar (FeNi29Co17)
materials.spec: Expansion matched to borosilicate glass and alumina, enabling hermetic glass-to-metal and ceramic-to-metal seals. Electronic packages, feedthroughs, vacuum windows.

materials.name: Nimonic 75
materials.spec: Solid-solution nickel-chromium (2.4951). Sheet for combustors, heat shields and exhaust parts: oxidation resistance to about 1000 °C, modest strength. Weldable.

materials.name: Nimonic 80A
materials.spec: Precipitation-hardened nickel-chromium (2.4952). Turbine blades, exhaust valves, high-temperature bolts and springs to about 815 °C.

materials.name: Nimonic 90
materials.spec: Precipitation-hardened Ni-Cr-Co (2.4632). Turbine blades and discs, hot springs and fasteners to about 920 °C.

materials.name: Nimonic C263
materials.spec: Ni-Co-Cr-Mo (2.4650). Combustors, casings and rings: formed and welded, then aged.

materials.name: Inconel 600
materials.spec: AMS 5540 sheet, AMS 5665 bar (2.4816). Furnace parts, heat shields and hot ducting. Good oxidation resistance; low strength.

materials.name: Monel 400
materials.spec: AMS 4544 (2.4360). Seawater, hydrofluoric acid and oxygen service: fittings, valves and fasteners. Good resistance to burning in oxygen.

materials.name: MP35N (cold worked and aged)
materials.spec: AMS 5844/5845 (35Co-35Ni-20Cr-10Mo). High-strength fasteners (260 ksi class) for corrosive service: highly resistant to hydrogen embrittlement and stress corrosion.

materials.name: Brass CZ121 (CW614N)
materials.spec: The free-machining brass: the benchmark for machinability at 100%. Fittings, valve bodies, turned components. Lead content is under regulatory pressure.

materials.name: Brass CZ106 (CW505L), cartridge 70/30
materials.spec: CuZn30, half hard (R410). BS EN 1652 sheet and strip, EN 12449 tube; UNS C26000. The most ductile brass: deep drawing, spinning, cartridge cases, bellows and instrument parts. Cold-worked parts can crack in ammonia (season cracking): stress relieve them.

materials.name: Brass CZ108 (CW508L), common 63/37
materials.spec: CuZn37, half hard (R410). BS EN 1652 sheet, EN 12163 rod; UNS C27200. The general brass for pressings, deep-drawn and spun parts, fasteners and electrical parts. Not resistant to dezincification.

materials.name: Brass CZ109 (CW509L), Muntz metal 60/40
materials.spec: CuZn40, alpha-beta, hot worked. BS EN 1652, EN 12163 and EN 12165; UNS C28000. Plate, tube plates, forgings and architectural parts. Dezincifies in water and seawater: do not use it for wetted parts.

materials.name: Brass CZ112 (CW712R), naval
materials.spec: CuZn36Sn1Pb. BS EN 12163, EN 12164 and EN 12165; similar to UNS C46400. Tin improves the resistance to seawater and to dezincification. Marine fittings, valve stems, condenser plates.

materials.name: Brass CZ114 (CW721R), high tensile
materials.spec: CuZn40Mn1Pb1AlFeNi. BS EN 12163, EN 12164 and EN 12165; similar to UNS C67500 (manganese bronze). Manganese, aluminium and iron give the strength of a mild steel: valve stems, gears, pump parts and marine shafts. Dezincifies in seawater: for wetted marine parts, use a DZR brass or an aluminium bronze.

materials.name: Brass CZ122 (CW617N), hot stamping
materials.spec: CuZn40Pb2. BS EN 12164 and EN 12165 (forging stock); similar to UNS C37700. The hot-stamping brass: forged valve bodies and fittings, then machined. Not resistant to dezincification; the lead content is under regulatory pressure.

materials.name: Brass CZ132 (CW602N), DZR
materials.spec: CuZn36Pb2As, heat treated. BS EN 12164 and EN 12165. Arsenic and the heat treatment stop dezincification. Fittings, valves and connectors in potable water and seawater systems.

materials.name: Brass CZ110 (CW702R), aluminium brass
materials.spec: CuZn20Al2As, annealed tube. BS EN 12449 and EN 12451 (heat-exchanger tube); UNS C68700. The classic seawater condenser and heat-exchanger tube: aluminium gives a protective film, and arsenic stops dezincification.

materials.name: Phosphor bronze CW452K
materials.spec: Excellent spring properties, fatigue resistance and corrosion resistance. Springs, electrical contacts, bellows, wear strips.

materials.name: Bearing bronze CC493K
materials.spec: Leaded tin bronze for plain bearings and bushes. Good embeddability and conformability, tolerant of marginal lubrication.

materials.name: Beryllium copper C17510
materials.spec: ASTM B441, RWMA Class 3. Lower beryllium than C17200 and much higher conductivity: resistance-welding electrodes, current-carrying springs, bushes. Beryllium dust needs controls.

materials.name: Aluminium bronze C63000 (CuAl10Ni5Fe4)
materials.spec: AMS 4640 (C63000), BS EN CW307G. Landing-gear and flap-track bushes and bearings, seawater fittings: high strength with good wear and galling resistance against steel.

materials.name: Copper C101 (Cu-ETP), half hard
materials.spec: BS EN CW004A (C101). Bus bars, earthing straps and heat spreaders. High conductivity, low strength; softens above about 200 °C.

materials.name: EPDM insulation (aramid filled)
materials.spec: Today’s default case insulation: low density, low conductivity, good ageing, bonds well. The fibre filler holds the char together under flow.

materials.name: EPDM insulation (carbon-fibre filled)
materials.spec: Tougher char for aft domes and other high-flow regions. Higher conductivity than aramid-filled grades.

materials.name: NBR insulation (silica filled)
materials.spec: Nitrile rubber insulation. Asbestos-filled grades were used before; asbestos is no longer used.

materials.name: Silicone insulation (silica filled)
materials.spec: Makes a char with much silica; flexible over a wide temperature range. Bonding needs special primers.

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy, quasi-isotropic laminate
materials.spec: Quasi-isotropic carbon/epoxy laminate, in-plane values. For a ply-by-ply analysis use the ply data and the lay-up.

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy, filament-wound case (hoop)
materials.spec: Hoop-direction properties of a filament-wound case laminate, for growth and strain estimates. Strength depends on the winding pattern.

materials.name: Composite propellant, HTPB type (illustrative)
materials.spec: Illustrative relaxed modulus, expansion and thermal properties of a composite propellant grain, as used on the propellant pages. Real values come from the propellant specification and tests.
